recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is. No core follow-up is needed unless TestReport is brought back into core or the external testing IG later loses either the required entered-in-error status or the separate result element.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive FHIR-core issue asking to resolve the TestReport build warning that every resource needs an entered-in-error status. The recorded resolution renamed TestReport.status to TestReport.result in SVN 10900, then re-added TestReport.status with completed, in-progress, waiting, stopped, and entered-in-error values in SVN 10912.
initial_application: Git commit f8ac640bcff2d110bf45e55e16ac7b0827c19137 corresponds to SVN 10900 and renamed TestReport.status to TestReport.result in the TestReport spreadsheet and example. Git commit 1684c2f3fda22aa108d076d930361a72fac58901 corresponds to SVN 10912 and re-added TestReport.status, report-status-codes, and an example status=completed/result=pass pair.
additional_context: The last core TestReport StructureDefinition before testing resources were removed retained TestReport.status as a required modifier code with entered-in-error semantics and TestReport.result as a separate required pass/fail/pending code. Current core no longer lists testreport in active source/fhir.ini [resources] and instead points to the HL7 FHIR testing IG, where the current TestReport definition still matches the FHIR-12717 split. FHIR-13069, a related TestReport.result audit, is already represented on the combined branch and supports the same current build-scope conclusion.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The requested source state was applied historically, persisted until TestReport left the core checkout, and remains correct in the current delegated testing IG definition; there is no active core TestReport source file to edit.

related_jiras.note: The existing combined-branch audit for TestReport.result modifier status confirms that TestReport moved out of active core source and that the current external TestReport definition is authoritative.
